nodes.title: SG-8.1 · Remove per-frame allocations and release resources
nodes.body:
Context: the Phaser scene in game/frontend/src/phaser and the engine in game/src have no update() loops, but the hover, focus and event paths allocate on every call. These are the event bus emit snapshot, a fresh payload per emit, closure-based find/findIndex/forEach, and a new hover event per hover. On shutdown, BootScene releases the fallback texture, input, store and event subscriptions, but not the loaded textures, the registered animations, the camera fade listener, running tweens, or sprite animation-complete listeners. Desired behavior: those paths reuse objects and every resource kind is released on shutdown. Expected result: gameplay is unchanged and each release is asserted by a unit test with Phaser mocked. Why: keeps long sessions and scene restarts free of garbage and leaks.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given repeated hover or focus changes, when events are emitted, then the same payload objects are reused and no new array or closure is created per call
- Given scene shutdown, when BootScene's SHUTDOWN handler runs, then loaded textures, created animations, tweens, the camera fade listener and sprite listeners are each released
- Given the same inputs as before, when the player hovers, focuses, interacts or transitions, then behaviour is identical to today and npm test and npm run typecheck pass in game/ and game/frontend/


## Scope
- In scope: events.ts emit, input.ts, engine moveFocus, frontend sync, SceneObject hover event
- In scope: preload.ts, characters.ts, transitions.ts, BootScene shutdown order and tween cleanup
- Out of scope: SG-8.2 dead-code removal and size/import rules
- Out of scope: SG-8.3 context.md and GDD
- Out of scope: backend/ and frontend/src/api/client.ts
- Preserve: Player-visible behaviour of the boys-room world
- Preserve: Phaser ~3.90.0 pin and phaser-pin guard test
- Preserve: Zustand store as sole owner of GameState
- Preserve: Every source file at most 200 lines, game/src never imports game/frontend


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays pinned at ~3.90.0
- No test deleted or skipped; tests mock only what is external
- No new features, content or juice
- game/src never imports from game/frontend


## Definition of done
- All three requirements delivered and wired through BootScene
- npm test and npm run typecheck pass in game/ and game/frontend/


## Non-functional requirements
- No per-call allocations on hover and focus paths


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Hover and focus sync paths reuse objects instead of allocating
nodes.body:
Context: createEventBus.emit copies the handler Set with [...set] on every emit; input.ts builds a new payload per emit and uses closure-based find; engine moveFocus and frontend sync use findIndex/forEach closures; SceneObject creates a hover event object per hover. Desired behavior: use cached handler arrays, reused payload objects, and index loops. Expected result: same observable behaviour with no per-call allocation. Why: required by SG-8.1.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a handler list that has not changed, when emit is called twice, then no new handler array is created and handlers still run on a stable snapshot
- Given two hover or focus emits, when the handler receives the payloads, then both are the same object with the current id
- Given moveFocus or sync is called, when it runs, then Array.prototype.findIndex and forEach are not invoked and focus results equal today's


## Scope
- In scope: game/frontend/src/phaser/events.ts
- In scope: game/frontend/src/phaser/input.ts
- In scope: game/frontend/src/phaser/buildScene.ts
- In scope: game/src/engine/buildScene.ts
- In scope: game/src/entities/SceneObject.ts
- Out of scope: Click-time availableActions allocation
- Out of scope: Changing event names or payload shapes
- Preserve: Handler order and subscribe/unsubscribe-during-emit semantics
- Preserve: Focus wrapping and hidden-object skipping


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays pinned at ~3.90.0
- Handlers must read payloads synchronously; payload objects are reused
- game/src must not import from game/frontend


## Definition of done
- Hover and focus paths free of per-call allocation
- Existing tests green


## Non-functional requirements
- Zero allocation on hover and focus paths


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Shutdown releases loaded textures and created animations
nodes.body:
Context: preload.ts dispose removes only the fallback texture; characters.ts creates global animations and never removes them. Desired behavior: remove each queued texture and created animation on shutdown, after sprites are destroyed. Expected result: nothing the scene added to the texture or animation caches remains. Why: SG-8.1 requires a release per resource kind.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a preloader that queued assets, when dispose runs, then textures.remove is called for each queued id that exists plus the fallback key
- Given characters that registered animations, when dispose runs, then anims.remove is called once per created key
- Given BootScene shutdown, when the handler runs, then characters and build are disposed before the preloader


## Scope
- In scope: game/frontend/src/phaser/preload.ts
- In scope: game/frontend/src/phaser/characters.ts
- In scope: game/frontend/src/phaser/BootScene.ts shutdown order
- Out of scope: Texture loading behaviour
- Preserve: Fallback texture behaviour
- Preserve: Restarting the scene reloads its assets


## Technical constraints
- Phaser ~3.90.0 APIs only: textures.remove, anims.remove


## Definition of done
- Release asserted per kind


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Shutdown releases tweens and listeners
nodes.body:
Context: transitions.ts registers cam.once(FADE_OUT_COMPLETE) and never removes it on dispose; character sprites keep once(ANIMATION_COMPLETE) listeners; nothing kills running tweens. Desired behavior: remove each on shutdown. Expected result: no tween or listener from the scene survives shutdown. Why: SG-8.1.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a pending fade, when transitions dispose, then cameras.main.off is called with FADE_OUT_COMPLETE and the stored handler
- Given character sprites with pending listeners, when characters dispose, then removeAllListeners is called on each before destroy
- Given BootScene shutdown, when the handler runs, then tweens.killAll is called


## Scope
- In scope: transitions.ts
- In scope: characters.ts
- In scope: BootScene.ts
- Out of scope: New tweens or effects
- Preserve: Transition fade behaviour and ignore-while-running rule


## Technical constraints
- Phaser ~3.90.0 APIs only


## Definition of done
- Each release asserted


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.summary: Replace allocating constructs in emit, input, moveFocus, sync and SceneObject hover
nodes.description: Change product code only so hover, focus and keyboard paths allocate nothing per call.
acceptance_criteria: emit iterates a cached array that is rebuilt only when handlers change
input.ts reuses one payload object per event and focusedId uses a for loop
moveFocus, sync and SceneObject hover use index loops and a reused event object
definition_of_done: npm run typecheck passes in game/ and game/frontend/

steps.action: Add a `snapshots = new Map<keyof T, Array<(payload: unknown) => void>>()`; in `on` and `off` call `snapshots.delete(event)` after changing the Set; in `emit` read `snapshots.get(event)`, or build it once with `Array.from(set)` and store it, then loop with an indexed for; in `clear` call `snapshots.clear()`.
steps.code: let list = snapshots.get(event); if (!list) { list = Array.from(set); snapshots.set(event, list); } for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) list[i](payload);
steps.expected: emit allocates no array while handlers are unchanged; handlers added during emit run from the next emit.

steps.action: Replace focusedId's `objects.find` with a for loop returning `objects[i].spec.id` of the first focused object or null. Declare `const focusPayload = { id: null as string | null }`, `hoverPayload` and `clickPayload` with the same shape; before each emit assign `.id` and emit the same object for focusChange, objectHover and objectClick.
steps.expected: Repeated emits pass the identical payload object.

steps.action: Replace `objs.findIndex` with a for loop computing `current`, and replace the final `objs.forEach` with an indexed for loop with the same focus/blur logic.
steps.expected: Same focus results with no closures.

steps.action: Replace both `objects.forEach` calls with indexed for loops (sync, then the focus/blur pass) keeping the conditions exactly.

Add a private field `hoverEvent = { objectId: '', over: false }`; in the handle.onHover callback set `this.hoverEvent.objectId = this.spec.id; this.hoverEvent.over = over;` and call `this.hoverListener?.(this.hoverEvent)` instead of building a literal.
steps.expected: Hover listener receives the same object each time.

steps.action: Add `const queued: string[] = []`; push `entry.id` in both the image and spritesheet branches; in dispose, after removing the loaderror listener, loop `for (let i = 0; i < queued.length; i++) if (scene.textures.exists(queued[i])) scene.textures.remove(queued[i]);` then `queued.length = 0`, keeping the existing fallback removal.

steps.action: Add `const createdAnims: string[] = []`; push `key` inside the `if (!scene.anims.exists(key))` block after `scene.anims.create`; in dispose after destroying sprites call `scene.anims.remove(createdAnims[i])` for each key and reset `createdAnims.length = 0`.
steps.expected: Each created animation is removed once.

steps.action: Reorder disposals to: inputLayer.destroy, unsubscribe, characters.dispose, build.dispose, transitions.dispose, then preloader.dispose last, nulling each as today.
steps.expected: Textures are removed only after the sprites using them are destroyed.
